To the most excellent son and our spiritual co-father, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Pope Paul.

Since the summit of royal power appears to be surrounded and fortified more by the strength of faith than by the weapons and might of warriors, what wonder is it, true and orthodox king of kings, if the exertions of your zeal do not cease to press more earnestly toward protecting the institution of God and the rule of Christian faith [Lambecius: “toward overthrowing”], and if, on this account, heavenly victory is granted to you and our Redeemer is believed to bestow prosperity upon your pre-eminent excellence?

When our envoys whom we had sent to your illustrious excellence returned to us—namely, John the subdeacon and abbot, and Pamphilus, regional defensor of your spiritual mother, our holy Church, together with your envoy Flavinus the chaplain—they brought us the honorable and most desirable letters of your Christianity. We received and reread it with immense joy, and at once its affirmation, affecting us like the fragrance of sweetness and healing us with the nourishment of salutary foresight, made us glad.

Moreover, most Christian king, most beloved son and spiritual co-father, your goodness made known how our envoys and those of the emperor had been received by you, and how you had endeavored to answer them concerning each matter which they had addressed to your illustrious eminence. You did not consent to receive them or answer them without the presence of our envoys, out of love for your patron, blessed Peter. Our own legates also reported these very things to us.

Although, on account of such an abundant sincerity of your heart, which you appear to possess toward your spiritual mother, the Church of God, and toward our weakness, we are able to render worthy recompense, nevertheless our protector is the Lord our God, who commanded you to reign and entrusted his holy Church to you for its defense; he can repay your excellence with a worthy recompense in the present and future life.

Accordingly, when we received the letters which the imperial envoys themselves had brought to you for purposes of pretense and deception, and which you had sent to us, we learned their contents. In this, the pious consideration of your goodness brought us the joy of exultation, because it is truly clear that you acted in this way not for human favor but out of fear of God.

You also made known to us more clearly, through those same letters of yours, what the aforesaid envoys of ours had argued and debated in your presence with the imperial envoys concerning the observance of the orthodox faith and the pious tradition of the Fathers. At the same time, your excellence, enlightened by God, granted that we should receive a copy of the letter which you sent to the aforesaid emperor, including the manner of your response [Lambecius: “the manner”] and the resolution of the petitions concerning what he had made known to you. You also informed us in detail how you answered those imperial envoys, how you sent one of them—namely Anthi, the spatharius [Idem: Anthinus; Grets.: perhaps Antimus or Anthymus]—to the royal city with your envoys, and how you retained the other, namely the eunuch Synestus, with you.

When we learned all that you had done for the exaltation of the holy Church of God and the defense of the orthodox faith, we rejoiced with great joy. These things are pleasing to us, just as it is certainly beyond doubt that you acted and answered in such matters not according to human counsel but under the providential direction of God. Truly, lord king, most Christian son and spiritual co-father, the Spirit of God enlightens the pious consideration of your inmost heart; and the one in whom the grace of the Holy Spirit overflows abounds in nothing except spiritual things, because the heart of your power, resting in the hand of God, undoubtedly inclines according to his good pleasure.

Through the same letters you sent us word that no flattering persuasion or abundance of promises could tear you away from the love and pledge of faith which you made to blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and to his vicar, our predecessor and brother, lord Stephen, pope of holy memory; rather, you would remain steadfast in that same charity and faith of your pledge to the end.

Indeed, most pre-eminent of kings, we have learned by experience and proved by deeds that you remain in that same pledge with firm and most powerful constancy to the end. We trust in you that, even if the abundance of all the treasures of the world were offered and granted before your sight [Idem: “brought”], it could in no way turn or bend your firm mind, impelled by God, toward another side [Idem: “bend it together”]. For the almighty Lord chose you above all the kings of the age and took pleasure in you, so that through your struggle the holy universal Roman Church of God, head of all the Churches and bulwark of the Christian faith, might stand liberated from the plots of its attackers. And behold, what the Lord decreed to accomplish through you from the foundation of the world has wondrously been brought to completion.

Therefore, after God, we have great confident hope in your royal eminence that the holy Church of God itself, and this most wretched and afflicted little province, may be more perfectly liberated from the treachery of its enemies, because the ancient enemy of the human race does not cease to assault the hearts of its enemies, so that they may hurl their customary plots.

But, good orthodox king, strive with your customary protection in battle, through God’s power, to crush their wickedness, so that the holy Church of God and its own people may be more perfectly freed from the savagery of their enemies, and so that, deservedly surrounded by the aid of the apostles, you may merit to attain in heaven the crown of reward stored up for you.

Accordingly, as you made known, we have sent your excellence our sign through your present envoy. Meanwhile, we also make known to your Christianity that Tassilo, duke of the Bavarians [Idem: “Tasilo, duke of the Bavarians”], is recognized to have repeatedly asked us to consent to send our envoys to your illustrious excellence, so that matters of peace might arise between you.

Accordingly, when the opportunity arose, we gladly appeared to send our envoys—namely, our beloved son, the presbyter Philip, and also our faithful Ursus [Lambecius: “our counselor and faithful man”]—to your presence, after the month of May had passed, specifically so that you should act according to whatever your will might be. When those envoys of ours hastened as far as Ticinum, Desiderius, king of the Lombards, seized by an adverse suspicion, did not permit them to proceed to your excellence, preserved by God [Idem: “to proceed on their way”]. Nevertheless, we transmitted the same letters which we were sending to you within this present writing to your Christianity.

Thus we considered it appropriate to make this known also to your Christianity, protected by God. When we reread the imperial letters delivered to you by the aforesaid Anthi the spatharius [Lambecius: “by the aforesaid Anthinus the spatharius”] and Synestus the eunuch [Grets.: “brought”], which you deigned to send to us so that we might examine their contents out of love for your patron, blessed Peter, we repeated the following point attached to them: your men and ours, who interpret those imperial words which have been or are being sent to you and to us, dare not interpret them according to what is written there, but falsely interpret one thing in place of another; and the envoys who hurry between the parties do not bring matters as they are charged to do, but, corrupted by the reward of acceptance, convey one thing in place of another [Note: “But the envoys”].

Let your excellence consider in this how great is the malice of the enemies: they utter against their own souls not what is true, but, through this crafty opportunity, wicked lies, trusting neither their own envoys nor yours nor ours. Just as you are satisfied with your men, so likewise we are satisfied with ours: they presume in no way to do this.

May almighty God, who searches heart and kidneys, satisfy the honey-sweet heart of your excellence, for none of our men has perpetrated such things, as they themselves assert. But that same emperor is vehemently angry about this [Idem: “the same”] and employs crafty pretexts because we did not at all remain silent in admonishing him concerning the establishment of the holy images and the integrity of the orthodox faith.

For in his own letters he asserts [Lambecius: “he asserted”] that our beloved son Christopher, the primicerius and counselor, had made those suggestions which we had repeatedly sent to him without our authority, as though we were unaware of them, and had reread one thing in place of another for his envoys and yours. In this we call God as witness and judge: it is absolutely not so. Our counselor has never done, or presumed to do, anything outside our will, because he was and remains the sincere and most proven faithful servant both of our predecessor and brother, lord Pope Stephen, and of us. We are satisfied with his spotless faith and firm constancy of heart.

Therefore, we believe that what is falsely reported to us is reckoned by God not as a reproach but as a crown of the prize; and for this reason the Lord is a helper to both of us, and we shall not fear what man can do to us. For after God, we shall have both a shield of protection and a weapon of strength in your illustrious excellence, enlightened by God.

Let your Christianity order its own envoys to investigate, and satisfy yourselves in every respect, because that same emperor asserted a lie against us: namely, that we had sent that suggestion, reading it together with those whom we sent and confirming what we had sent. Nevertheless, you appear to possess with you the copy which we sent to you.

With these matters set forth, bending our knees together with all the people of God [Idem: “the Lord our true God, maker of the heavens and earth”], we beseech the true Lord God, maker of the poles of heaven, to grant us a long life in the present age together with a great victory over our enemies [Col. 1151C], and to grant eternal joys to your excellence, as well as to the most Christian queen, your daughter and our spiritual co-mother, your most beloved wife, and to your sweetest children, the most excellent kings Charles and Carloman, kings of the Franks and patricians of the Romans. May heavenly grace preserve your excellence unharmed.

## LETTER VIII

Likewise, a copy of the letter of the same pope to the lord King Pippin, sent through the presbyter Peter, containing the embassy [Grets.: “legation”] of Bishop Remedius [Idem: “and of Andegarius”] and Count Audecarius, describing how they received from Desiderius, formerly king, part of the rights belonging to blessed Peter, prince of the apostles [Lambecius: “received”], and how he promised to render the remaining rights.

[Note: Grets., Summary 20, Baronius and the Centuriators.]

To the most excellent son and our spiritual co-father, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Pope Paul.

That your excellence has been proved worthy of merit through good works by heavenly judgment has already been demonstrated openly by the result of the things accomplished, since, having obtained from above a share in divine wisdom, you are plainly shown to have more effectively merited the scepters of royal eminence through heavenly blessing [Idem: “more efficaciously”].

Therefore, since your exaltedness does not doubt that this grace has been sent to you by almighty God, you strive with all your efforts to please the one who bestowed it and, by divine prompting, your excellence, to be protected by God, does not cease to contend with the eyes of its heart for the struggle which it has drawn forth as its own—namely, for the holy universal Church and the vigor of its exaltation—setting before itself the heavenly rewards promised for such labor by blessed Peter, prince of the apostles and keeper of the keys of the kingdom of heaven. There, joy is found not in human glory among human beings, but in divine happiness among the angels, a happiness never to be lost.

Rejoice and be glad, most fortunate king, because, with God’s consent, through your struggle your holy spiritual mother, the universal Church of God, rescued from the plots of its enemies and exalted, triumphs. And the orthodox faith, untouched by the arrows of heretics, stands firm through your zeal and the arm of your strength.

For this reason you have been made blessed and just in all your works, sweetest son and spiritual co-father, most victorious and excellent king. We make known [Lambecius: “We indicate”] to your exalted Christianity that recently, when your most faithful men had joined us—namely, your beloved Remedius, and Autharius, the most glorious duke [Idem: “Andegatius”]—it became clear that an agreement had been reached between them and Desiderius, king of the Lombards: throughout the whole coming month of April of this thirteenth indiction [Lambecius: “the twelfth”], he was to restore to us in full all the rights of your patron, blessed Peter, prince of the apostles—namely, all the patrimonies, rights, places, boundaries, and territories of various cities belonging to the Roman commonwealth [Col. 1152C].

Accordingly, that king of the Lombards is recognized to have rendered us part of those same rights, and he professes and entirely promises that he will also render us all the remaining rights. Therefore, the aforesaid Desiderius, king of the Lombards, earnestly begged us to make this known to your excellence, protected by God, through our apostolic reports.

And behold, just as we make this known through these apostolic words to your exalted and most sublime Christianity, protected by God, our liberator after God, so we are sending to your lofty sublimity, inspired by God, our beloved son Peter the presbyter. We ask that you kindly receive him with your customary regard and deign to send him back to us with effective and favorable news concerning the perfect and complete justice in the various causes of your patron, blessed Peter, prince of the apostles.

If, however, they—both the aforesaid King Desiderius and his Lombard people—remain in the pledge which they profess and promise, and if everything is restored to us by them according to what has been agreed and according to the terms contained in the covenants [Lambecius: “the agreements of the pacts”], then we shall make known to him the merit of your excellence, which is to be preserved by God [Idem: “the merit of the matter”].

Therefore, beseeching you, we ask, earnestly entreat, and even adjure you, most excellent and most Christian king, most beloved son and spiritual co-father, by almighty God and blessed Peter, who anointed you king, to order that everything pertaining to the exaltation and the fuller liberation of the holy Church of God and of this province redeemed by you be carried out and completed more perfectly, just as you promised to blessed Peter and to our predecessor, the pontiff of holy memory, our lord and most blessed brother, Pope Stephen.

Thus may he grant that you possess the promised and displayed crown of reward from the hand of our merciful almighty God; may his grace surround you, together with your sweetest wife, the most excellent queen, your daughter and our spiritual co-mother, and your beloved children—namely, the exalted kings [Lambecius: “likewise”]—and may he grant you to possess the summit of the present kingdom and the triumph of victory, and to enjoy eternal joys in the heavenly kingdoms with the saints. May heavenly grace preserve your excellence unharmed.

## LETTER IX

Likewise, a copy of the letter of the same pope to the lord Pippin, glorious king, sent through Bishop George, containing thanksgiving for the liberation of the holy Church of God; and in a postscript he asks that he might be worthy to receive his son, who had then been born, from the sacred font of baptism.

[Note: Summary 19, in Baronius and the Centuriators.]

To our most excellent son and spiritual co-father, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Pope Paul.

The transmission of letters ordinarily refreshes the mind by its very nature [Note: [Col. 1153D] Lamb., “always refresh by visitation.”] and becomes, in a certain sense, an occasion of affection. Since, therefore, the sincere love of spiritual sons willingly sustains paternal affections, it is fitting that we fulfill with the greatest eagerness what the affection of a pure conscience demands. And although the infrequency of messengers, owing to the length of the journey, hinders the performance of the duties of paternal love, whenever an occasion of necessity arises we do not cease to visit your most excellent Christian devotion through letters sent back and forth. We embrace you with our customary honor [Note: [Col. 1153D] Same, “embracing them in greeting, so that we may in some measure behold in alternating letters those whom we cannot see present with bodily eyes.”] [Note: [Col. 1153D] Grets., “it seems that ‘visit’ should also be restored here.”] so that, by the usefulness of correspondence, we may in some measure behold in writing those whom we cannot see present with bodily eyes [Note: [Col. 1153D] Same, “those whom.”].

Thus, with God enlightening all things, report has spread everywhere the merits of your excellence [Note: [Col. 1154D] Lamb., “of your excellence illumined by God.”], so that, from the deeds accomplished by it, they are laudably displayed to all. Therefore, insofar as the assertion of our mouth has force, by bearing witness through extended praise and returning thanks to your eminence, we judged it appropriate to send to your splendid, God-inviting [Note: [Col. 1154D] Same, “imitable.”] footsteps the most holy and reverend brother and fellow bishop of ours, George, whom we have entrusted to report individually to your God-protected sublimity every necessity concerning the interests of your spiritual mother, the holy Church of God, and of this province redeemed by you.

But we ask God—and earnestly beseech you, most gracious king, our son and spiritual compater, and, after God, our liberator—to command that this messenger of ours be received with the kindly and customary look of welcome and commended to your favor. May you deign to apply a suitable and prompt response to our petitions, which concern the exaltation of the holy Church of God, especially the reward of your soul and your eternal memory, by lending ears of your goodness moved by God [Col. 1154B]. For, most exalted of kings, most beloved son and spiritual compater, almighty God willed you to be present as the liberator of His holy Church through the hands of blessed Peter, so that, through your customary protection, the fullest salvation and redemption of His holy Church and of this province might advance.

We pray our Lord God to order your deeds by His mercy in such a way that, while enjoying prosperity, your excellence may govern the affairs of the kingdom for a long life [Note: [Col. 1154D] Same, “with victory.”], and reach the rewards of eternal promise in security, together with your most sweet wife, the most excellent queen, our spiritual co-mother, and your distinguished children, that is, the kings; and may that same almighty God grant that both of you rejoice forever with the saints in the heavenly kingdoms. May heavenly grace preserve your excellence unharmed.

## EMBOLUM

Meanwhile, most exalted of kings, it has been brought to our knowledge that, by God’s will, almighty God has granted for the exaltation of His holy Church a new king from your loins [Note: [Col. 1154D] Lamb., “the Lord.”]. We have been lifted up by the greatest joy at his birth. Therefore we earnestly ask you to permit us to receive this, your most distinguished son, from the most sacred laver of baptism [Col. 1154D] [Note: [Col. 1154D] Same does not have “greatest.”], so that the twofold grace of the Holy Spirit [Note: [Col. 1154D] Same, “may arise among us”] may be in our midst, and the joy of a double festivity may arise for us.

[Col. 1155A]

## EPISTLE X

Also, an exemplar of a letter of the same pope to Lord King Pippin, sent through the Lombards [sic], containing thanksgivings and abundant blessings for his life and safety, and likewise for those of Lord Charles and Carloman, in his noble letter, desiring to obtain assistance, with many adjurations against the Lombards; and in an embolum [Note: [Col. 1155D] Grets., “and in the embolum”; Lamb., “and in the embolum there is contained the mandate which.”] there is contained the mandate that he sent to the presbyter Marinus concerning the title of Chrysogonus and the books that he sent to him.

[Col. 1155A]

[Note: [Col. 1155D] Grets., Summary 18, in Baronius and Centuriatus.] To our most excellent son and spiritual compater, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Pope Paul.

The bearer of the letter hastening to us—namely, the illustrious man, the faithful messenger of your eminence—brought us a nectarous and flower-bearing report of the words of your excellence protected by God [Col. 1155B]. Examining more carefully the attached page and what its text said, we understood every detail. For, recognizing in the very utterances of your sublimity the desirable joy of your health, and a joy embraceable above all such delights [Note: [Col. 1155D] Lamb., “embraceable”], we were released into the overflowing rejoicing of our heart, especially because we were granted to learn what our heart had desired.

Afterward, when our messengers returned from your God-imitable footsteps and brought back those very tidings of your prosperity [Note: [Col. 1155D] Same, “from you”], a twofold joy of exaltation was inserted into our heart in our reply. For when the joy of your enlarged prosperity had sounded in the ears of all the priests and clergy, and even of the nobles and the rest of the people, they, filled with boundless joy and rejoicing, exulted with us in the Lord, having learned the safety of their own defender after God.

Moreover, most excellent son protected by God, and spiritual compater, we have learned by experience that you burn with vehement love for the love of the prince of the apostles, blessed Peter, and for our affection [Note: [Col. 1155D] Same, “that you burn with love for our affection”], especially since that letter of your excellence is seen to have been written with the pen of charity. Indeed, the tongue had dipped from the heart what it poured onto the page.

Therefore, excellence protected by God, we return great thanks to you, since divine clemency, through the intervention of its prince of the apostles, has most kindly appointed you, the defender and helper, as king of His holy Church. Let your eminent care persist in securing the complete redemption of this province and the exaltation of this holy Church. Hence, together with all the people entrusted to us, we implore the mercy of our Lord God, that He may protect you by His grace; and, granting you victory from heaven, may He subject all barbarian nations to your footsteps [Col. 1156A], and grant you to earn the governance of the kingdom for a long life, together with your most sweet wife, the most excellent queen, our spiritual co-mother, and your and our most beloved children, Lord Charles and Carloman, most powerful kings, and Lady Gisla, most excellent; and may He grant you the joys of eternal life with the elect of God.

Therefore I ask and beseech you, most excellent son and spiritual compater, and adjure you by almighty God and the body of blessed Peter, whose most faithful servant you are, and I earnestly entreat you with the greatest supplications: command that you carefully retain in your holy, God-inspired, honey-sweet heart [Note: [Col. 1156D] Grets., “having understood”] what our lord and brother, the most blessed Pope Stephen, of holy memory, admonished you by God’s will and asked you to accomplish [Col. 1156B]. Command that you fulfill and bring to effect everything he requested of you with such a terrible adjuration, and remain in that charity and friendship, so that you may deserve to obtain the perfect reward and the crown of our complete redemption laid up with the just Judge, the Lord our God, who anointed you king [Note: [Col. 1156D] Same, “and the joys of eternal blessedness”], together with the joys of eternal blessedness with the saints and elect of God, while, by freeing the Lord’s people more completely and defending the holy Church of God, you preserve it unharmed from the malice of those who rage [Note: [Col. 1156D] Same, “when you have presented it unharmed from the malice of those who rage”] before the divine majesty.

For this reason, most gracious king, we place great hope after God in the pledge of your promise, which you bestowed upon blessed Peter, together with all the people of this province redeemed by you.

[Col. 1156C] All the priests and clergy of this holy Catholic and Apostolic Roman Church greet the Christian devotion of your excellence. The entire senate of the nobles and the assembly of diverse peoples also greet you, wishing together with us to rejoice for a long time in your abundant prosperity and overflowing joy, and to exult in the Lord God our Savior. May heavenly grace preserve your excellence unharmed.

## EMBOLUM

In another letter, your excellence protected by God sent word to us, as to a father who truly desired your good, asking that we should grant to your most beloved and faithful presbyter Marinus the title of your protector, blessed Christ-martyr Chrysogonus, together with everything belonging to it [Col. 1156D]. You asked that a mandate concerning this be sent to you [Note: [Col. 1156D] Same, “and the mandate be sent to you”]. Because of your affection, and because the aforementioned title’s most holy and beloved presbyter Marinus is both your faithful servant and ours, we have had a mandate concerning that title, together with all its urban and rural places and possessions, written out for you and confirmed by our hand, and we have sent it to your eminence to be conveyed by the bearer of this letter [Col. 1157A].

We have also sent to your preeminence as many books as we could find: namely, an Antiphonary and a Responsory, together with Aristotle’s *Art of Grammar*, the books of Dionysius the Areopagite, *Geometry*, *Orthography*, *Grammar*, all the Greek-language writers, and also a nocturnal horologium.

## EPISTLE XI

Also, an exemplar of a letter of the same pope to Lord King Pippin, sent through Wulfard [Note: [Col. 1157D] Lamb., “through Wlfhard”] and his associates, containing abundant praises, and concerning the apostolic messengers and the Greeks staying in Francia [Note: [Col. 1157D] Same, “here, Francia”], as well as concerning George [Note: [Col. 1157D] Gret. Cent., “Bishop Gregory”] and Peter.

[Note: [Col. 1157D] Same. Summary 16 in Baronius and Centuriatus.] To our most excellent son and spiritual compater, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans [Col. 1157B], Pope Paul.

We send the desires of our heart and the affection of our inmost breast, presenting to the holy Church of God the vows arising from the support of the benefactions of your excellence [Note: [Col. 1157D] Same, “the support”]: perpetual salvation to your exalted Christian devotion; to your most excellent and most gracious daughter and compater, the best queen; likewise to your most beloved and distinguished sons, our sons beloved in Christ, Charles and Carloman, most excellent kings of the Franks and patricians of the Romans; and also to all our most reverend brothers and bishops beloved by us, to the presbyters, and likewise to the religious abbots; and to all the nobles, judges—namely, dukes and counts—and to the entire people of the Frankish kingdom protected by Christ and subject to you [Col. 1157C].

All our most holy brother bishops, presbyters, the entire order of the clergy of your holy and spiritual mother, the Roman Church, and the assembly of the nobles, the great and lesser Roman aristocracy, and the whole Roman people [Note: [Col. 1157D] Same, “the nobles and the entire Roman people, great and small”], remaining with us and embracing you in the kiss of charity, likewise send you perpetual salvation, earnestly beseeching the divine clemency with us for the joy of your life and safety and for victories granted to you from heaven.

Indeed, it is your due, most excellent son, our defender and liberator after God, that we repay the affection of customary honor, utter words of greeting with the greatest earnestness, and proclaim most fully those things that pertain to the immense praise of your kingdom [Note: [Col. 1158D] Lamb. and Grets., “of exaltation”] and to the salvation of your soul [Col. 1157D].

When our messengers returned—namely, Peter, regional notary of our holy Church, and John, mansionarius of the basilica of the confessor, your protector blessed Peter—having joined with your messengers, Wulfard and his associates [Note: [Col. 1158D] Same, “Wlfhard”], they brought us the honorable and greatly desired words of your preeminence [Col. 1158A]. When we had read them in the gathering of our brother priests, clergy, and the entire assembly of the lay order, and when our messengers and yours had reported to us what you had entrusted to them concerning the steadfastness of your unchanging mind and the integrity of your purity, which you appear to possess for the hope of the holy Church of God and the orthodox faith, we were immediately filled with immense joy. Raising our eyes to heaven and extending our palms, we offered boundless thanks to our almighty God and to your excellence [Note: [Col. 1158D] Same, “we offer”], singing that angelic praise of His divine power on account of your merits [Note: [Col. 1158D] Gret., “Luke, chapter 2”]:

> Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will.

For the minds of the faithful could not believe otherwise, good king, than what we have perceived to have been accomplished by you through their works [Note: [Col. 1158D] Lamb., “than what we have perceived from the works”]: you rejected human persuasions and empty promises out of regard for this consideration, and preferred to place nothing above the love and struggle that you maintain for blessed Peter [Note: [Col. 1158D] Same, “which”]. But, regarding all earthly profits as mud trampled underfoot, you make it your concern to please him and to obey his commands with all your strength.

And therefore, behold, good king, exalted son and spiritual compater, you have stored up for yourself infinite treasures in the starry vaults, where rust cannot prevail and moth cannot consume what is to be bestowed upon the just. Since the works of your exalted excellence shine so wonderfully, who could in any way doubt you, when you strive to preserve eternally, with his right inviolate, what you promised to blessed Peter and sought to grant for the forgiveness of your sins [Col. 1158C], and when you commit this to your own great exhortations, you who are to be preserved by yourselves and by God? Therefore it is exceedingly necessary for us, and for all our people, to trust that you, your offspring, and the entire kingdom of the Franks will remain firmly constant in this purpose and in such an unchanging steadfastness of mind. For, as your excellence has made known to us, we know whom we have believed, and we are certain.

Concerning our purity and affection toward you and toward the entire kingdom of the Franks protected by God, we believe that you are already fully satisfied. For greater assurance, calling upon the God of heaven as witness, we confess that we shall remain in that charitable affection which you promised to preserve until the end of the age with our lord and brother, the most blessed Pope Stephen, of holy memory, and through him with all his pontifical successors—you, your offspring, all your descendants, and the entire kingdom of the Franks. We likewise confess that we and our pontifical successors shall remain in it for the exaltation of the holy Church of God and the defense of the orthodox faith [Col. 1159A]. [Note: [Col. 1159D] Lambec., “And no.”] No condition of affairs will ever be able to separate us from this confirmation of charity.

Your Christian devotion therefore sent us word that our messengers, yours, and those of the Greeks who had returned from the royal city were being detained with you, while you gathered your priests and nobles in order to deliberate or determine what should be answered concerning the matters sent to you. Indeed, we cannot expect any other answer from you than those things known to pertain to the exaltation of the holy spiritual mother of your Roman Church, the head of all the Churches of God, and of the orthodox faith [Note: [Col. 1159D] Same, “the head of all the Churches of God”]. And since what you once offered to blessed Peter, in return for eternal life [Col. 1159B], ought by no reasoning to separate you from his right and authority [Note: [Col. 1159D] Same, “nothing through you … should be separated”], we know that no persuasive tale prevails with you, since you firmly retain divine words and apostolic teachings joined to your heart.

And behold, just as through your letters and ours, and through your messengers, you have supplied us with the greatest grounds for confidence, we await from you joyful news concerning this matter and rejoice, as is customary, in your gracious purpose of mind.

Your exalted Christian devotion also asked through the same letters that we grant permission for Bishop George and Presbyter Peter to remain in your service [Note: [Col. 1159D] Same, “to remain”]. Let your most excellent goodness know that long ago we obeyed your wish in this matter. Through Andrew, your most religious messenger, we recognized that, as you requested, we granted them to you in written apostolic letters that we sent [Col. 1159C]. We informed you that, whether it was your will to retain them or to release them, you were to act concerning them accordingly [Note: [Col. 1159D] Same, “whether to retain or to release”]. Therefore, even now, we leave it to your discretion: do with them as you wish, whether retaining or releasing them, since they have once been granted to you by us. Would that they might be agreeable in your service!

For this reason, inform us what we ought to do concerning the episcopate of the aforementioned George and the church entrusted to the aforesaid Peter, lest, after being admonished further, they fall into excessive negligence.

[Col. 1159D] Meanwhile, according to your command, we have retained in these regions two of your messengers, namely Wulfard and his companion, for the interests of our holy Church, your spiritual mother.

Your excellence also made known that you had sent Desiderius, king of the Lombards, word that he should return to us the boy Saxulus, who had fled from us. But let your Christian devotion know—for I think you also have learned this—that during the past autumn [Note: [Col. 1159D] Lamb., “at the time of autumn”], or at that time, the same Desiderius, king of the Lombards, came to the threshold of the apostles for the sake of prayer and, bringing that same boy with him, handed him over to us [Col. 1160A] [Note: [Col. 1159D] Gret., “had arrived”].

When that king spoke with us concerning the completion of justice between the parties, it was agreed [Note: [Col. 1160D] Lambec., “so that our men”] that, as your messengers and his proceeded through the various cities, the judgments themselves should be prepared. And behold, by God’s favor, we have both rendered and received judgments from the regions of Benevento and Tuscany. In the duchy of Spoleto, while our messengers and those of the Lombards are still present there, we have likewise rendered and received judgments in part. They are also striving in every way to complete fully between the parties the remaining matters.

In an embolum, your excellence protected by God informed us that you had admonished the kings of Naples and Gaeta and constrained them to restore to your protector, blessed Peter, the patrimonies situated there in Naples [Note: [Col. 1160D] Lamb., “to be constrained, for the purpose of restoring them”], and to grant customary permission to the elect who wish to hasten to this apostolic see to receive episcopal consecration [Note: [Col. 1160D] Same, “and to grant permission to the elect”; Grets., “and to grant permission to the elect, etc.”]. Therefore we return the greatest thanks to you for this and for everything.

With these matters stated beforehand, may almighty Lord God encompass you with His continual protection, rescue you from every adversity, and subject all barbarian nations to your footsteps. May He grant you to enjoy this present kingdom happily for many years together with your beloved wife and distinguished sons, and grant you eternal life to possess with the saints. May God preserve you unharmed, most excellent son.

## EPISTLE XII

Also, an exemplar of a letter of the same pope to Lord King Pippin, sent through Bishop George, Presbyter Stephen, and Radbert, as messengers; containing thanksgivings for the defense of the holy Church of God, and in which the aforesaid pope asks that Lord King Pippin return Desiderius’s hostages to the king and confirm the treaties of peace with him.

[Note: [Col. 1160D] Grets., Summary 13, in Baronius and Centuriatus.] To our most excellent son and spiritual compater, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Pope Paul.

When almighty God repeatedly pours forth so abundant a mercy of His goodness upon the human race [Col. 1160D], it must be considered what can be repaid to His divine power, or what praises in songs human frailty can offer for His forbearance. Indeed, though we have been raised up by so great a benefit of His, although our merits in no way support us, we shall render melodic thanks to His power [Note: [Col. 1160D] Lamb., “our psalm-writing thanks to Him …”]. Nevertheless, according to the admonitions of the psalmist [Note: [Col. 1160D] Grets., “Psalm 115”], “I will take up the cup of salvation and call continually upon the name of the Lord,” asking: [Note: [Col. 1160D] Same, “Tobit, chapter 13”] “You are great, O Lord, and great are Your works.” For my soul magnifies the Lord; flesh and tongue bless Him. For He has looked upon, yes, looked upon our lowliness, and has raised me to so distinguished a pontifical eminence, not because our merits pursued it.

Therefore, since by His favor I have been established as a watchman of souls by the mediator between God and human beings, the apostolic care entrusted to me urges, exhorts, and wholly compels me, without ceasing, to secure the salvation of God’s people with devout zeal and to preach peace among all nations with great steadfastness of heart. For those who have preferred to preach it fearlessly earn the grace of blessedness. It is written: [Note: [Col. 1161D] Grets., “Matthew, chapter 5”] “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.” And again: [Note: [Col. 1161D] Same, “to the Romans, chapter 10”] “How beautiful are the feet of those who proclaim peace, who proclaim good things” [Col. 1161B].

Indeed, most excellent son and spiritual compater, because almighty God, having you predestined from your mother’s womb [tuae, “your”] [Note: The transmitted text is uncertain here; the reading may be “from your mother’s womb.”], blessed you and anointed you king, He appointed you as the defender [te, “you”] and liberator of His holy Church. Therefore, through these apostolic letters, we have hastened to entreat your gracious excellence concerning matters that concern the welfare of that holy Church of God.

Let your most excellent goodness know that our most excellent son, King Desiderius, came to the threshold of the apostles peacefully and with great humility. We spoke with him concerning the salvation of both parties, and he promised us that he would restore the city of Imola [Note: [Col. 1161D] Lamb., “Imulas”], on the condition that we should send our messengers to your excellence and that he should receive his hostages whom he appears to have there with you [Col. 1161C], and that you should strive to confirm peace with him.

Therefore we ask you, most excellent son and spiritual compater, to command that those hostages be returned to our aforementioned son, King Desiderius, to confirm the treaties of peace with him, and to live with him in great friendship. Thus, with God’s assent [Note: [Col. 1162D] Lamb., “with God’s favor”], the people of God on both sides may dwell in great security and the tranquility of peace during your joyful times, so that almighty God may deign to preserve you for a long life upon the throne of the kingdom.

For this reason we have sent our most faithful messengers, namely our most reverend and most holy brother and fellow bishop, George, and our beloved son, Presbyter Stephen [Col. 1161D], together with your messenger Rodbert, to your excellence protected by God [Note: [Col. 1162D] Same, “for we sent them in fact”], so that they may recount these very matters to your eminence.

With these matters stated beforehand, we ask divine mercy to deign to preserve you for long and joyful ages, remaining upon the throne of the kingdom in devout works [Note: [Col. 1162D] Lamb., “clinging to works”], and to grant you eternal life. May heavenly grace preserve your excellence unharmed.

## EPISTLE XIII

Also, an exemplar of a letter of the same pope to Lord King Pippin for the defense of the holy Church of God, containing thanksgivings and abundant blessings for the preservation of the integrity of the orthodox faith.

[Col. 1162A]

To our most excellent son and spiritual compater, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Pope Paul.

Since the holy spiritual mother and your particular universal Church of God is known to have been raised up by so great a benefit of your most exalted excellence and by the assistance you have generously supplied, what human tongue could suffice to return thanks for the merits of this gracious work of yours? And although human understanding cannot repay this, nevertheless He who is powerful, almighty and invisible, our Lord God, by whose ordinance your royal power stands confirmed, will, through the intercession of the sacred prince of the apostles, blessed Peter, repay you with a worthy reward in the present life and in future blessedness [Col. 1162B].

This is especially so since you appear, most excellent son and spiritual compater, to be a very strong defender of the holy orthodox faith and of the pious tradition of the venerable fathers. For these very reasons, you honor and strive to defend the orthodox faith which they venerate; you will always have it as your helper (*astrix*), and certainly heavenly victory will be granted to you against the ranks of your adversaries.

Meanwhile, since we burn with great affection toward your excellent eminence protected by God, we have diligently arranged to discharge toward your sublimity the duty of visitation and greeting, exalted son and spiritual compater.

We wish your excellence to remember that recently you sent us word that we should strive to live in the love of peace with Desiderius, king of the Lombards. If that most excellent man remains in the true love and faith that he promised to your excellence and to the holy Church of God at Rome, then we too shall remain with him in firm charity and stable peace, observing that teaching of the Lord’s command [Note: [Col. 1162D] Grets., Matthew, chapter 5]: “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.”

We therefore inform your most Christian equity that it has been agreed between us and the same king of the Lombards that we should meet together in the city of Ravenna to complete certain interests of our spiritual mother, the holy Church, and to deliberate concerning the malice of the Greeks, who daily threaten to enter that city of Ravenna. When we have met there together, whatever we say, or whatever the merits of the matter require, we shall make known to your most excellent eminence protected by God.

For the rest, we pray divine clemency to preserve and protect your most excellent Christian devotion, for the perfect exaltation of the holy Church of God and the defense of the orthodox faith, through long and prosperous times [Col. 1163A] [Note: [Col. 1163D] Grets., “long”; Lamb., “ages”], upon the throne of royal power, together with your most sweet wife, the most excellent queen, our spiritual co-mother, and your most beloved children; and to grant you the eternal joys of the heavenly homeland to possess. May heavenly grace preserve your excellence unharmed.

## EPISTLE XIV

Also, an exemplar of a letter of the same pope to Lord King Pippin, containing blessings; and the aforesaid pope asks that Lord King Pippin send his messengers to the region of Rome [Note: [Col. 1163D] Lamb., “and inform him concerning his health”], inform him of his health and safety and of how he had fared on the journey, and tell him how the Lord had delivered his enemies into his hands and humbled them beneath his feet.

[Col. 1163B] [Note: [Col. 1163D] Grets.: Summary 11, in Baronius and Centuriatus.] To our most excellent son and spiritual compater, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Pope Paul.

Whenever the spiritual endeavors of God’s faithful are reported, the minds of those who hear are immediately kindled in the love of God and in the divine commandments. They are moved to proclaim most fully, for the praise of God, the merits of heavenly consideration [Note: [Col. 1163D] Lamb., “are aroused to contemplation, and therefore, most powerful of kings, it is pleasing to proclaim most fully for the salvation and praise of God the merits of your pious reflections, etc.”], and to commit them to the testimonies of Scripture, which are to endure forever [Note: [Col. 1163D] Grets., “are kindled, or something similar”]. Through your cooperation and assistance, the exaltation of the Church of God and the defense of the orthodox faith are secured [Note: [Col. 1163D] Same, “are advanced”]. For this reason you are recognized as blessed and praiseworthy before God and human beings in all things, most Christian king, and the name of your goodness shines, written in the sight of the divinity.

For although a period of time has passed during which we have neither been granted a report of your safety nor been able fully to learn what was happening concerning you or how you fared on the journey on which you departed [Col. 1163C], the affection of our desire is stirred by an excessive heat of anxiety to learn this diligently, especially since adverse reports concerning those regions have been announced to us by our enemies and yours. Therefore a great desire clings to us to learn the joys of your safety, to rejoice in your prosperous endeavors, and to learn of the defeat of your enemies.

For this reason we ask you to command that, as we desire, you make us certain through your messengers of your prosperity and joy. For your health is our prosperity, and your exaltation is without doubt our joy and immense security [Note: [Col. 1163D] Same and Grets., “and divine”]. Accordingly, we beseech the worthy power of God that He, our protector, together with His angels, may deign to guard and govern your most excellent Christian devotion, so that in the heavenly kingdoms, together with the saints and elect who pleased God from the beginning of the world, you may abundantly obtain your reward.

[Col. 1164A] We desire that your excellence protected by God inform us more fully what you appear to be doing concerning yourself and your Christian people, and how our God has humbled your enemies and ours. As we have said, command that you make us certain, as we desire, of your prosperity and joy. May heavenly grace preserve your excellence unharmed.

## EPISTLE XV

Also, an exemplar of a letter of the same pope to Lord King Pippin, containing thanksgivings and concerning his health, as well as that of Charles and Carloman [Note: [Col. 1164D] Lamb., “as well as that of Charles and Carloman, and concerning”], and concerning the presbyter Marinus and Ravenna, namely, how evil plans are being devised against it.

[Note: [Col. 1164D] Grets.: Summary in Baronius and Centuriatus.] To our most excellent son and spiritual compater, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans [Col. 1164B], Pope Paul.

To your eminent excellence, protected by God, the bearer of this letter has delivered messages filled wholly with sweetness and affection. We received them with profound reverence and recognized more clearly everything contained in them. Among other things, most excellent son, your lofty benevolence toward us became known: by the merciful favor of our God, you are healthy, safe, and unharmed, together with your most excellent children, our spiritual sons Charles and Carloman, great kings, and the lady Bertrada, most sweet queen, our spiritual godmother [Grets. and Lamb.: “your most sweet wife and spiritual godmother”], as well as our most noble daughter Gisela.

When we learned this, we returned great and innumerable praises, by the judgment of heaven, to the Lord our God, King of kings [Lamb.: “we offered”], since, in accordance with what we desire with the greatest longing, we have been permitted to learn of your well-being. For this reason we earnestly implore our Lord God to grant that, through the course of many years, we may rejoice in your complete health, since your safety is our rejoicing and your prosperity is unquestionably our joy.

It was also written in your royal letters that you wished us to inform you whether the safety or integrity of the holy Church of God, our unworthiness, or the people entrusted to us was under attack [same: “the people entrusted to us”]. For this we give great and innumerable thanks to almighty God and to your excellence, because, as is truly fitting for a most Christian man and genuine worshiper of God, your excellence does not shrink from visiting the Church of God and its people. Yet this is accomplished not through our merits but through divine mercy, since all things prosper concerning the holy Church of God, our unworthiness, and the people entrusted to us [same: “toward”]. For this we shall ask the God of heaven, the giver of every good thing [Lamb.: “who is for you”], to repay you for this outstanding and pious work, and for the great benevolence and solicitude that you are recognized as showing toward the holy catholic and apostolic Church of God and its particular people [Grets.: “its own people”].

Your most Christian excellence also wrote that your envoys had informed you that certain malicious persons and purveyors of lies had spread in these regions the report that, if any necessity should befall us, you would wish to provide us no assistance [Lamb.: “would not be able to provide”]. We have had, and have, no hesitation whatsoever concerning this wicked statement, since, by divine mercy, after God we place great hope and trust in you. We recognize that, with God’s favor, there will be no obstacle from any quarter to your granting defense and assistance to the holy Church of God and its particular people, in accordance with what you promised and pledged to the blessed apostle Peter through our predecessor of blessed memory, our lord and brother, for the remedy of your soul and the forgiveness of your sins. With the Lord’s assent, we believe that this will remain firm and strong for all time.

As for what your most Christian excellence directed to us—that, if any of your adversaries or despisers should come to us, we should in no way associate with them or enter into their company—far be it from us to do such a thing, since your enemies are certainly enemies of the holy Church of God and of us. Truth therefore bears witness that, wherever we recognize your friends, we desire to welcome and embrace them as friends and faithful servants of the holy Church of God; and wherever we find your enemies, we truly reject and pursue them as enemies of the holy Church of God and our own enemies. For your friends are friends of the holy Church of God and of us, while those who plot hostility against you are plainly shown to be enemies of the holy Church of God and of us.

Concerning your envoys and ours, who hastened together toward the royal city [Lamb.: “who”], your distinguished excellence asked us to inform you whether we had learned anything from them. It is certainly not unknown to us that, because of the severe harshness of this winter season, no one arriving from those regions has announced to us how matters stand with them [same: “whether they are”]. Therefore, at present, we do not know what truthful report to give you concerning them.

Your most Christian excellence also wrote to us that the presbyter Marinus had at last been restored to his former honor, in accordance with what we requested when we sent word to you. We call God as our witness that we sent to you on his behalf for no other reason than the tears and daily lamentations that his mother does not cease to shed. She is also deprived of sight; for this reason we sent to you, so that you might release him in your presence. You had—and have—no grievance against him, nor do we, except solely concerning his wicked malice, by which, moved by evil and perverse audacity, he presumes to act against the holy Church of God. But concerning this matter, as we wrote to your excellence in our earlier letters, let it be in your judgment and power what you wish to decide regarding him. We have no concern about him, except, as we have said, that you should deal with him according to your will. Your excellence also instructed us to tell you whether the same Marinus had sent us any letters. In truth, we say that he has never sent us a letter since he departed for your presence [same: “from the time”]. We would in no way have concealed this from you had it happened [same: “we would not have been able to conceal it from you”].

Meanwhile, we considered it appropriate to inform your excellence of what has reached us from the faithful of the holy Church of God and from our own people—that is, from the region of Ravenna—since the enemies of the holy Church of God, of us, and of your excellence do not cease day and night to devise how, with God opposing them, they might prevail and overcome us [same: “to deliberate”]. We have also enclosed below in this letter the very written reports that we received from there, so that, learning the true nature of the matter, you may recognize that they do not in any way desist from their evil purpose and customary wickedness. Therefore, most Christian good son and spiritual godfather, command that you labor and contend with the greatest exertion, so that the good work you have begun may be completed through you, and so that the holy Church of God and its particular people may obtain complete liberation and remain secure from the plots of their enemies.

Finally, we ask the divine mercy of our God to preserve you for the course of many years upon the throne of your kingdom, together with your most excellent children, our spiritual sons Charles and Carloman, kings of the Franks and patricians of the Romans, and also the lady Bertrada, most excellent queen, our spiritual godmother and your wife, as well as Gisela, most noble girl, our spiritual daughter, for the exaltation and defense of the holy Church of God and of its particular people. We desire for a long time to learn of the joys of your prosperity and to implore God’s immense clemency on your behalf. May heavenly grace keep your excellence safe.

## LETTER XVI

A copy of another letter of the same pope, addressed to the lord king, concerning the defense of the holy Church of God and a conference with King Desiderius in the city of Ravenna.

[Grets.: Summary in Baronius and Centuriatus.]

To the most excellent son and our spiritual godfather, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Paul the pope.

Since the holy spiritual mother and your particular universal Church of God is recognized as having been relieved by the great benefit of your most exalted excellence and the assistance you generously supplied, what human tongue could suffice to render thanks for the merits of this good work of yours? And although the capacity of human understanding cannot repay it, nevertheless he who is powerful—the almighty and invisible Lord our God, by whose ordering your royal power has been firmly established—will, through the intercession of the sacred prince of the apostles, the blessed Peter, repay you with a worthy reward in the blessedness of the present life [Grets. and Lamb.: “and of future blessedness”], especially since you appear to be a most courageous defender of his orthodox faith and of the pious tradition of the venerable fathers, most excellent son and spiritual godfather. For this reason, the orthodox faith itself, which you reverently honor and strive to defend, will always be your helper, and heavenly victory will certainly be granted you against the armies of your adversaries.

Meanwhile, because we burn with great affection of love toward your distinguished excellence, protected by God, we have diligently fulfilled the duty of visiting and greeting your highness, distinguished son and spiritual godfather. We wish your excellence to remember that you recently sent us word that we should strive to maintain an association of peace and affection with Desiderius, king of the Lombards [Lamb.: “we wish your excellence to remember that you recently sent us word”]. If that most excellent man remains in the true faith and affection that he promised to your excellence and to the holy Church of God at Rome, then we too shall remain with him in steadfast charity and stable peace, observing the teaching of the Lord’s command: “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God” [Grets.: Matthew, chapter 5].

We therefore inform your most Christian excellence that it has been agreed between us and the same king of the Lombards that we should together present ourselves in the city of Ravenna to complete certain matters concerning the welfare of your spiritual mother, our holy Church, and to deliberate concerning the malice of the Greeks, who daily threaten to enter that city of Ravenna. When we have appeared there together, whatever we discuss, and whatever the merits of the matter require, we shall make known to your most excellent excellence, protected by God.

Finally, we pray the divine clemency to preserve and protect your most excellent Christianity, in prosperous times and throughout the ages, upon the throne of royal power, together with your most sweet wife, the most excellent queen, our spiritual godmother, and your beloved children; and to grant you the possession of the eternal joys of the heavenly homeland. May heavenly grace keep your excellence safe.

## LETTER XVII

A copy of another letter of the same pope, addressed to the lord King Pippin, concerning a certain monk, Acosma, sent by the patriarch of Alexandria [Lamb.: “addressed,” and likewise elsewhere].

[Grets.: Summary 7 in Baronius and Centuriatus.]

To the most excellent son and our spiritual godfather, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Paul the pope.

Since, through the preceding grace of the Holy Spirit, the love of God has inflamed the heart of your benevolent and distinguished excellence, it is plainly evident, most excellent king preserved by God, that you adhere to pious pursuits. And since we see such abundant grace accumulated in you, a source of confidence in you has been granted entirely to us and to all Christians: we see that you will carry out with the full effort of your mind whatever pertains to the worship of God and the observance of the orthodox true faith.

Among these matters, most exalted son and spiritual godfather, if anything reaches us, we gladly report it to you as an orthodox king and defender of the Christian faith. We inform you that, after your envoys had already departed, a ship arrived to us from the regions of Africa. In it came a certain monk, Acosma [Lamb.: “Cosmas”], sent by the patriarch of Alexandria with letters. We have sent you a copy of them, radiant excellence, for your inspection, so that you may learn what is sent to us concerning the integrity of the faith by the Eastern bishops and other nations, and so that your heart may rejoice in their devotion, which appears to be directed toward the commandments of God. Since your mind is intent upon the study of pious reflection, we certainly believe that you will rejoice greatly if we make known to you what pertains to the integrity of the faith. May the holy orthodox faith itself, which you reverently honor, preserve you with long life and victory in the present life, and grant you eternal joys to possess with the saints. May heavenly grace keep your excellence safe.

## LETTER XVIII

A copy of the general letter of the people and senate of Rome, addressed to the lord King Pippin, containing thanksgiving and concerning the letter that the lord King Pippin sent to that people regarding the preservation of their faithfulness toward the holy Roman Church of God and toward the lord Paul the apostolic pope.

To the most excellent and most eminent, God-appointed, great and victorious Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans: the entire senate and the whole community of the people of the city of Rome, preserved by God.

If human understanding should wish to weigh inwardly, in the mind, the purpose of your deeds, nothing, as we believe, can be considered worthy of repaying them in kind or of being rendered in this temporal life. Only those things should be regarded as repayment to you by the just Judge, our Lord God, which “eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the human heart,” which he has prepared for those who love him. This is indeed a worthy repayment for you, since through your struggle the holy Church of God and the orthodox faith of Christians are recognized as having been defended, and the means of salvation for all of us have constantly been secured.

And since, most eminent lord king, our God has deigned to accomplish the redemption of his holy Church and of us all, it is fitting that we should sing of the wonders of his works, singing with one voice together with the prophet: “For your works, O God, have been magnified. You have made all things in wisdom; the earth is filled with your wonders” [Grets.: Psalm 183]. “For who can speak of the mighty deeds of the Lord and make all his praises heard?” [same: Psalm 105]. The heavens rejoice and the earth exults because our Lord has bestowed upon his holy Church such a defender, through whom the name of the Lord is glorified with confidence in his holy hall.

We received the letters sent to your most eminent and Christian benevolence with great reverence, and in receiving them we rejoiced as though we were actually beholding your excellence. They filled us with the twofold joys of a festival, since we learned in full measure of your happiness. Nothing is sweeter to us in this life, lord king, than to rejoice in your prosperity, since your safety, after God, is our security.

In those honey-sweet letters, your excellence also took care, through your provident admonition [Lamb.: “to admonish us by your providence”], to warn us that we must remain steadfast and faithful toward the blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and the holy Church of God, and toward your most blessed and angelic spiritual father, appointed by God, our lord Paul, supreme pontiff and universal pope. We rejoiced exceedingly at such a wise admonition from you. O how, through divine inspiration, the inward power of our hearts overflows within us, your faithful servants! Truly, lord king, the Spirit of God dwells in your honey-sweet heart; therefore you have striven to admonish those who wish you well with such a salutary counsel.

We, most eminent of kings, stand as steadfast and faithful servants of the holy Church of God and of the aforementioned, thrice-blessed and angelic spiritual father, our lord Paul, supreme pontiff and universal pope. He is our father and excellent shepherd, and he does not cease daily to contend for our salvation, just as his brother of holy memory, the most blessed lord Pope Stephen, did, cherishing and wisely governing us as rational sheep entrusted to him by God. He is exceedingly gentle and truly merciful in all things, having become an imitator of the blessed Peter, whose office he holds and whose vicar he is.

We, most excellent and most Christian lord king, have firm confidence in such a promise of yours. Yet we earnestly beseech you, and, as though prostrate at your royal feet in your presence, we ask—indeed, blessed Peter himself, through us, approaches your excellence—that you command, most gracious of kings and our defender after God, that you continue to contend and act in your customary manner, so that the perfect exaltation of the holy Church of God and the defense of our orthodox faith and of all of us may be secured [Grets.: “may be provided”].

We also ask this before the living God, who commanded you to be anointed king through his apostle, the blessed Peter: command that the expansion of this province, wrested by you from the hands of the nations, be completed, and remain in the good work you have begun, so that we may be able to live in great security and peace, and that you may thereby receive in heaven an eternal reward obtained through prayer. For, after God and the blessed Peter, we possess our greatest hope in the arm of your most powerful kingdom. We trust in the mercy of our almighty God that this very hope of ours will most abundantly bring forth the fruit of your works.

Hear, lord king, the supplication of all who wish you well, and gladly incline your ears to this very request of ours. May the Lord hear you in all your petitions. For after God you are our defender and helper. Even if all the hairs of our heads were turned into tongues, they would not be able to offer adequate thanksgiving for such great benefits of yours. Nevertheless, insofar as our mind is able, we proclaim the praises of your glory among all nations.

Therefore, raising our eyes and extending our hands toward heaven, we implore our Lord God with immense prayers to cherish you with his grace, sending before your face an angel of his power as your champion, who, conquering all your adversaries, may subject them to your feet, enlarge the boundaries of your kingdom, and grant you victory from heaven. May he grant you, the most excellent lady queen, and your illustrious children, the most excellent kings, the possession of the royal throne throughout ages and the happiest times, for the perpetual and everlasting security of the holy Church of God and of us, and may he grant you abundant eternal joys of reward with the saints and elect. May heavenly grace keep your excellence safe.

## LETTER XIX

A copy of another letter of the same pope, addressed to the lord King Pippin, containing thanksgiving for the exaltation of the holy Church of God and a request that he send his envoy to Rome.

[Grets.: Summary 6 in Baronius and Centuriatus.]

To the most excellent son and our spiritual godfather, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Paul the pope.

Things done at our expense [Lamb.: “for our support”] cannot be erased by any forgetfulness. How much less can those things be consigned to oblivion that are done to the praise of the Redeemer, our Lord God, of his most sacred Church, and of the blessed Peter, prince of the apostles? Neither the length of time nor changing circumstances consigns them to oblivion; rather, they remain continually proclaimed as examples of piety, to the glory of heavenly power and of its faithful [same: “declared; as, most excellent son”].

Know, most excellent son and spiritual godfather, good orthodox king, that your lofty and pious work shines, illuminated before the angels of God in heaven, and remains honorably proclaimed throughout the whole world among all nations. For through your help, after God, and through your excellent struggle, your spiritual mother, the Church of God, has been rescued from the plots of its enemies, and the orthodox Christian faith has been defended against its attackers. Therefore rejoice in the Lord and be glad, most gracious king, because the name of your excellence shines, inscribed in the book of life, in the sight of God.

Meanwhile, since such a great capacity of desire presses upon our heart—that we should become joyful and certain concerning your prosperity—we considered it appropriate to fulfill toward your excellence the duty of sending the reports of the holy Church of God. Nothing is sweeter or more pleasant to us in this life than to rejoice in your prosperity in the Lord, since, as we have always written, your safety is the exaltation and true defense of the holy Church of God and of the faith [Lamb.: “exists, as we have often written; and therefore, because”]. Since we are separated from one another by bodily distance, we nevertheless desire through our reports to be joined spiritually to you by mutual love.

Therefore, we earnestly beseech your excellence, as we requested in our earlier letters, to command that your most faithful envoy be sent here to us in Rome. He should remain with us because of the plots of the enemies, and through him we shall be able to inform your excellence, as the outcome of the matter requires, of its true condition [same: “therefore we have expressly sent”].

For this reason we have now sent to your excellence, preserved by God, Peter, first defender of our holy Church, a most faithful envoy. We have instructed him to write to your benevolence concerning all apostolic affairs. We ask that you receive him with a cheerful spirit and accept him in every matter for love of your patron, the blessed Peter, prince of the apostles. May you deign to lend the ear of your benevolence to our requests and command that he be released to return to us with successful results and joyful reports.

With humble supplication we ask you, good orthodox king, to be for us, after God, a steadfast protector and defender, remaining consistently in the good and pious work of redeeming the holy Church of God that you have begun. Your most excellent Christianity is well aware of how great and of what kind is the impious malice of the heretical Greeks, who eagerly devise and plot how, with God opposed to them, they may humble and trample down the holy catholic and apostolic Church and destroy the orthodox faith and the tradition of the holy fathers [same: “meditating and plotting”].

But you, good and most powerful king, deign, as a true orthodox Christian, to resist those same impious heretics with courage, and, as is your custom, defend the holy Church of God and the orthodox faith of Christians through your God-protected and suitably ordered assistance. For after God there is great confidence in your excellence and in the arm of your most powerful kingdom. We believe that, with God cooperating, this hope of ours, remaining firm, will reach the desired goal, so that in return the just Lord our God may grant you reward in the present and future life, through the intercession of the blessed prince of the apostles, for love of whom you contend in his causes. Rejoicing, as is your custom, in your pious purpose [same: “of your pious”], may we be able to sing together with the prophet in a harmonious voice:

“Save, O Lord, the most Christian King Pippin, whom you commanded to be anointed with holy oil by the hand of your apostle, and hear him on whatever day he calls upon you.”

Along with these prayers, we also ask his piety to grant that, through a long old age, your excellence may enjoy the power of the kingdom, together with the queen protected by God, our spiritual godmother [Lamb.: “and our spiritual godmother”], and your beloved children, the lords Charles and Carloman, most exalted kings of the Franks and patricians of the Romans, and the most noble lady Gisela; and that he may grant you the blessedness of the heavenly kingdoms to enjoy eternally. May heavenly grace keep your excellence safe.

## LETTER XX

A copy of another letter of the same pope, addressed to the lord King Pippin, asking about his health and safety, and also concerning his envoys who had been sent to the royal city.

[Grets.: Summary 5 in Baronius and Centuriatus.]

To the most excellent lord and our spiritual godfather, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Paul the pope.

In our letters and messages previously sent through Droctegand [Lamb.: “Uulfhard”] and Vilkard, beloved of God, your envoys to the most faithful king, we earnestly asked your distinguished excellence to agree to make us more certain and happier concerning your complete health and concerning the journey on which you had set out—how the Lord had dealt with you. But when such a long period had elapsed and we had learned no series of replies from you on this matter, our spirit was greatly distressed.

Then, however, through pilgrims arriving from various regions at the thresholds of the apostles, we learned that, by God’s favor, you, most excellent son and spiritual godfather, had returned safely to your own land. At this our spirit was lifted with great joy.

Therefore, sending these present apostolic words as a gesture of visitation, we earnestly ask that your exalted excellence quickly make us joyful by informing us of your complete health and safety, most Christian son and spiritual godfather, and of how matters stand with you, your most excellent daughter, our spiritual godmother, and your distinguished sons [same: “your sons”]. May our spirit exult with the greatest joy, since we burn with an intense desire continually to learn of your well-being and rejoice in your happiness. For your safety is the exaltation of your holy mother, the Church, and your prosperity is proved to be our joy.

Therefore, most excellent son and spiritual godfather, good and excellent king, until now we have been able to learn no reliable report concerning our envoys who departed from the royal city. As soon as we are able to learn the truth of the matter, we shall immediately send a reply to your distinguished excellence.

With these matters stated, we ask the God of heaven to grant you the enjoyment of a long life in the present world and of the government of the kingdom, together with the most excellent queen, your daughter and our spiritual godmother, the most Christian queen and your sweetest wife, and your beloved children, our sons, those same distinguished kings and patricians of the Romans; and may he make us participants in the kingdom of heaven, permitting us always to rejoice in your complete well-being. May heavenly grace keep your excellence safe.

## LETTER XXI

A copy of another letter of the same pope, addressed to the lord King Pippin, concerning the presbyter Marinus, his wicked counsel, and his consecration.

[Grets.: Summary 4 in Baronius and Centuriatus.]

To the most excellent son and our spiritual godfather, Pippin, king of the Franks and patrician of the Romans, Paul the pope.

Your most Christian excellence is fully aware of how our presbyter Marinus [Lamb.: “who is there”] remains with you, wishing, through wicked action against the holy Church of God and the orthodox faith, with God opposed to him, to join with a certain imperial secretary named George in devising counsels contrary to our see and likewise to yours [same: “to impose”]. The emperor himself also made this known to your excellence, protected by God, through his letters.

Therefore, since the blessed apostle and prince of the apostles Peter has deigned to choose and confirm your most Christian benevolence as defender of the orthodox faith, champion of his flock, and liberator of the Christian people, we make this request and earnestly beseech your distinguished benevolence, excellent king and spiritual godfather, to command our most holy brother Bishop Wulchar [same: “Wilchar”] that he himself, in our place, consecrate this same presbyter Marinus as a bishop. You should arrange for him to be ordained in one of the cities in your regions, wherever your most wise and distinguished excellence foresees it, so that, remembering the crime he has committed, he may repent of having acted wickedly. Otherwise—God forbid—the ancient enemy of the human race, finding his mind wandering, might raise him up as though to a height and then utterly destroy him with savage violence in whatever way he could.

Rather, as we trust in your most gracious excellence and in the God-given expansiveness of your illustrious heart, may your distinguished excellence deign to lend an ear to this request of ours, so that he may remain secure concerning this matter and so that we may command unceasing prayers to the Lord God of heaven for your immense joy and the happiness of your well-being. Farewell.

## LETTER XXII

A copy of another letter of the same pope, addressed to the lords Charles and Carloman, kings, containing thanksgiving and concerning the letter sent by them, and instructing them always to contend with their lord father for the defense of the holy Church of God.

[Grets.: Summ. 17. Baronius and Centuriatus mention three letters to Charles and Carloman outside their regular order.]

To the most excellent sons, the lords Charles and Carloman, kings of the Franks and patricians of the Romans, Paul the pope.

How splendidly you adorn the summit of royal glory with the brilliance of honor is plainly evident to everyone, since, being born of distinguished lineage, you appear to be adorned with pious works and worthy character. Thus you possess one grace of this divine gift through your ancestry, and enjoy another through your deeds. Nor is it surprising that your nobility excels with such distinguished insignia of glory, since it is written: “The generation of the upright shall be blessed” [same: Psalm 3].

We glorify and praise the clemency of our God, who has bestowed upon you such great grace of the Holy Spirit. He had indeed predestined you before you came forth from your mother’s womb, since “those whom he foreknew, he also predestined; those whom he predestined, he also called; and those whom he called, he also magnified” [same: Paul’s Epistle to the Romans, chapter 7]. Truly the Lord has magnified his mercy over you, anointing you as kings through his apostle, the blessed Peter, and appointing you defenders of his holy Church and of the orthodox faith. In this good work, you have become participants with your most Christian father; for this, a worthy reward will be granted to you with him in the heavenly kingdoms, and you will be counted among the entire company of the saints.

Meanwhile, Peter, our envoy and first among the defenders, returned to us and brought the letters that you sent. When they had been read again, our heart was filled with great joy.
